spec.title: vscode-extension PROP-001: The `vscode-extension` project type - overview and module map

status.comment: the module of the vscode-extension project type, written 2026-11-01 from DESIGN-002 (vibevm/vibespecs/research/design/DESIGN-002-vscode-extension-type.md) and the public Extension API; the facts of the one measured specimen are recorded in the consumer's own repository and are not restated here (common/PROP-004 NO-CONSUMER-PRODUCT-IN-THE-TOOL). Implemented by the campaign campaigns/vscode-extension-type as the package @codkit/type-vscode-extension

p.VSX-TYPE-IS-AN-ANSWER-SET: `vscode-extension` is the project type (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-TERM`) that carries the tool's knowledge of a Visual Studio Code extension repository as an upstream: a package - alone in its repository or one workspace package of a monorepo - whose `package.json` is at once the product manifest and the host contract, built by the package manager the repository names into a bundle, packaged by `vsce` into a `.vsix`, and looked at by launching a VS Code-based host with it. It is the fourth official type, the third real one, and the first to answer the eleventh question of the contract, the preview.

p.VSX-TYPE-FROM-FACTS: Every fact of this module is derived from the public Extension API and from one real specimen measured on 2026-11-01; the specimen's facts, with their `path:line` citations, live in the consumer's repository, and this module states them at the level of the family. A fact the specimen did not establish is marked as an open question in DESIGN-002, not guessed.

p.VSX-SPECIMEN-UNNAMED: The specimen and the product built on it are named nowhere in this repository - not in this module, not in the type package, not in its fixtures, which model a synthetic extension of their own (`common/PROP-004` `NO-CONSUMER-PRODUCT-IN-THE-TOOL`, DESIGN-002 D8). The isolation grep over the tool repository prints zero before every commit of the campaign.

p.VSX-MODULE-MAP: PROP-001 the type and this map; PROP-002 the configuration of the type, upstream identity and tree layout; PROP-003 the layers - the manifest overlay, the locale manifests, the entry module, the absences, and how the rebrand toolkit maps onto the layers; PROP-004 build, watch, lint, test, packaging and the preview recipes; PROP-005 the upgrade advisory, the conventions and the generators - the feature skeleton, the brand table with its hook, and the leftover guard.

p.VSX-CAPABILITIES: Declared, for every patch set of the family: `config-overlay` (the extension manifest and the locale manifests, no `dev-channel`), `entry-module` (the activation module), `build-channels` (the bundle and the type check watchers), `upgrade-advisory` (readers over the manifest), `gen-brand` (the brand table, the hook and the leftover guard) and `preview` (the development host and the installed artifact). Not declared, each absence an answer of PROP-003 and PROP-004: `own-extensions`, `service-override`, `dev-channel`, `brand-images`, `runtime-library`. A verb that needs an undeclared capability refuses with `CK-E-TYPE-CAPABILITY` (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-CAPABILITY-REFUSAL`).

p.VSX-CONFIGURED-TYPE: The type is configured (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-CONFIGURED`): its answers are functions of `typeConfig` (PROP-002 `VSX-TYPE-CONFIG`), so it answers `configure` and the engine asks the result everything afterwards. The capabilities are the same for every configuration, so `configurableCapabilities` is empty and `codkit types` prints a true matrix with no patch set in reach.

p.VSX-STANDARDS-PACKAGES: The first version of the type names no vibe package of its own: `codkit standards load` delivers the universal `standards` and `agent-skills` to a patch set of this type and nothing else. A catalogue of this family's seams - the manifest overlay, the funnels of the translations, the contribution points, the webview, the telemetry switch - is `seams-vscode-extension`, deferred by name in the campaign plan (DEF-3); when it ships, it is delivered beside the universal set and to this type alone, as `seams-theia` is for its family (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-014#STD-PACKAGES-OF-THE-TYPE`).

absences.title: 4. What the family does not have

p.VSX-ABSENCES: No own extensions: an extension has no extension host of its own to materialize a second extension into. No service override: the family has no uniform service registry - an extension composes itself in its activation module, which is where own code enters (PROP-003 `VSX-ENTRY-MODULE`). No dev channel: the host reads the manifest from the extension root and there is no sidecar it reads instead, so the overlay is materialized into the tree for packaging and for a preview alike (PROP-003 `VSX-NO-DEV-CHANNEL`). No brand images in the first version: the icon files the manifest names are replaced as resource files, and a regenerated icon set from masters waits for the first product that asks (DESIGN-002 D6, campaign DEF-2). No runtime library: the one shared module of the toolkit, the brand transform, is generated self-contained into the own layer (PROP-005 `DECISION-VSX-BRAND-TRANSFORM-SELF-CONTAINED`). No build-time stamps by default: nothing of the family bakes a commit or a date into the bundle; a product that wants one declares it (PROP-004 `VSX-STAMPS`).
